title: High-Temperature Oxidation and Phase Stability of AlCrCoFeNi High Entropy Alloy: Insights from In Situ HT-XRD and Thermodynamic Calculations

questions.broad: For high-entropy alloys intended for high-temperature applications, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain their ability to develop and retain a protective oxide layer that provides oxidation resistance? Specify what governs the behaviour and why, a controlled comparison that would reveal it, the observations expected relative to a baseline, the applicable boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.
questions.problem_constrained: For CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain whether a stable, coherent protective oxide layer forms and persists during exposure above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere, rather than developing unstable surface oxides that crack or spall? Specify what governs the behaviour and why, a controlled comparison against a defined baseline, the predicted differences, the applicable exposure and material-state boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a falsifying observation.
questions.expert_context: For CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain whether a stable, coherent, slow-growing protective oxide layer forms and persists above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere, rather than cracking or spalling? Earlier work investigated CrFeCoNiX and CrMoTiAlY (Y = Ta, Nb, or W) alloy systems and reported that some compositions developed unstable surface oxides prone to cracking and spallation, while the underlying physical causes remain unresolved. Given the requirement for an environmentally stable, chemically inert barrier and prolonged structural integrity, specify what governs the behaviour and why, a controlled comparison against a defined baseline, the predicted observations, the relevant composition, material-state, exposure, and service boundaries, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.
